Chapter 9: When You Really, Truly Don’t Want to Cook
You know those days when even making the simplest meal just feels... impossible? The fridge is full, the pantry’s packed, but your motivation? Nowhere to be found. It’s so easy to fall into that trap of guilt, wondering—why does something so basic have to feel so hard sometimes?
Picture this: a young professional, totally overwhelmed by work and life, just staring at the kitchen, frozen with indecision. She knows she should cook. But the thought of chopping, stirring, and then cleaning up? It’s all just too much. So, instead of forcing herself, she gives herself permission to take a break. Maybe she grabs a bowl of cereal, orders some takeout, or just has toast with peanut butter. And guess what? The world doesn’t end. Slowly, that feeling of guilt starts to fade away.
Most of us don’t realize—it’s perfectly okay not to cook sometimes. That pressure to always be “good” or “responsible” can weigh you down, but honestly, everyone needs a break now and then. Sometimes, real self-care is about taking the path of least resistance. Your meal doesn’t have to be homemade to count.
Here’s something worth paying attention to: there’s real value in keeping a few “emergency” meals on hand. I’m talking about those lifesavers that take almost no effort—like frozen dumplings, instant noodles, or a simple can of soup. These aren’t failures; they’re lifelines for when your energy just isn’t there.
Think about a parent, completely wiped out after a sleepless night, microwaving a frozen meal for herself and her child. Sure, it’s not what she’d planned, but it’s enough. Just taking the time to feed herself, even in the simplest way, is still an act of care.
Over time, you start to realize: the goal isn’t to cook every single meal, every day. It’s about finding a balance that actually works for you. Listening to what you need in that moment, and letting go of the guilt when things don’t go as planned.
The kitchen will still be there tomorrow, waiting for you, ready for another try.
